# Operator-arrow first-source study

This informed study precedes an ordinary operator/capability/Meaning decision
for Issues 83/44/45/46/57/89. It adopts no syntax or mathematical guarantee.
The [original context](context.md) and [chronology clarification](context-clarification.md)
distinguish drafting, later reads, actual observations and metadata repair.

Twelve complete first projects are frozen in attempt-01 with explicit schema-2
edition-2026 manifests. first-files.json binds every original source and manifest.
All 24 first text/JSON observations rejected before native checking: private
host entries, missing explicit imports, or deliberately unadopted syntax. Those
authoring mistakes are real retained failures, not language or model statistics.
attempt-02 changes visibility and retains its accidental `unitary pub fn`
ordering mistake. attempt-03 adds explicit finish/split imports and repairs that
order. Source, manifest, raw events, executed drivers and native invocation logs
remain beside each observation. Nothing executes a command read from a record.

The final 24 observations agree between text and JSON. Five projects obtain one
actual native invocation in each format: identity, scalar-phase, first-order
unitor, observation and the existing static endomorphism. Seven reject before
native checking: four syntax candidates, a same-width wrong-tree provider, a
false Unitary assertion on preparation, and the current preparation profile
limit. summary.json records every observed classification and identity.

The preparation control is `fn entry(q:Q<Unit>)->Q<Bit>{finish(q);init0()}`.
Its source body has principal Iso. Auto selects finite Raw because the current
hierarchy profile explicitly excludes Iso roots; Raw then rejects Q<Unit>.
This reproduces already recorded unfinished profile parity. Removing that
type restriction alone is insufficient: Raw has no pure Unit introduction or
elimination opcode, and its independent replay currently tracks Q<Bit> owners.
Observing discard cannot substitute for finish, and a source assertion cannot
change the inferred effect. No fallback or checking relaxation was added.

Current `Op<A, M>` uses its second slot for Meaning, so a proposed `Op<A,B>`
codomain spelling collides with that existing syntax. `Op<A -> B>` and quantum
closure candidates currently reject in parsing. These failures establish no
capability, capture, adjoint or controlled-arrow rule. The eventual decision
must cover distinct input/output trees, isometries, complete instruments and
independent Meaning/capability evidence together.

The selected Rust/native binaries and 184 Rust sources remain identical across
all three observation phases. This is a check-only study, with at most one
physical input qubit, no maximum-size generation and no independent semantic
oracle execution. In particular scalar-phase check success is not an observed
complex-amplitude or exact-phase theorem. The original intended equations remain
obligations in cases.json. General source preservation, QS/PR/quantitative RS and
EXACT remain pending; both admitted scoped QLV1 meanings remain unchanged.
